title: AI animated archival photographs for a historical film
summary: Giovanni Abitante used unnamed generative video tools to animate archival photographs for I Am an American, a short film that received 2025 awards; no source measures its effect on viewers.
source_collection: University of Texas AI Opportunity Inventory
account: Giovanni Abitante used generative video to animate Dorothea Lange’s photographs and reconstruct scenes for I Am an American, a short film about the wartime incarceration of Japanese Americans. In a July 2025 festival interview, he described AI as a production technique within a project that depended on archival research and writing. The MetaMorph AI Film Award named the film runner-up in its 2025 Mockumentary category. The Perugia Social Film Festival lists a 2025 Best Documentary award from the Burano Artificial Intelligence Film Festival. The Perugia festival’s program lists the film and its recorded testimony. The festival included the film in its first showcase of generative-AI shorts, held from 24 September to 4 October 2026. The evidence establishes a completed creative work and its public exhibition. No source measures an improvement in historical understanding or audience engagement.
purpose: The filmmaker used AI to create moving images from historical photographs for a completed film.
system: Generative video tools used in I Am an American
taxonomy_note: The recorded benefit is a completed creative output. Historical accuracy and educational effects are not independently evaluated.

ratings.reason: The filmmaker reports that AI let him animate archival photographs of events with few surviving film records, which he says that he could not have done without it. The film received awards in 2025, and no source measures any effect on viewers.

ai_role.statement: AI generated motion and reconstructed scenes. Archival research, writing, editing, and testimony also contributed. The reviewed external sources do not establish the exact models.
